lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what restoring a unit's condition removes from its next-period event count, which is only the part of its event rate that has grown since the condition was last restored, per unit of an exposure that drives every event; the latest counts mix that growth with each unit's own base and with an exposure that moved in opposite directions across areas, so the units that look worst were selected on a high-exposure year or on a high base the restoration cannot touch, and the units with the most to gain look ordinary.

lineage.driver_concrete: FLISR's 2026 sustained interruptions avoided are the customers it restored within five minutes, with the sequences the ADMS archive dropped on storm days read back from the outage record's restoration steps and the devices' own operation records, less the customers its own switching put out: closes onto mislocated faults, and the receiving feeder's midline recloser tripping on the combined load hours after a summer transfer, coded no cause found; the controls whose batteries cannot crank at the design cold are read from weekly self-test sag against temperature, since spring and autumn functional tests pass them; and summer auto-transfer stays off on the directions whose reinforcement the capital works history says will not be in service by the 2027 summer.

lineage.fate: returned at review 2026-11-13 after upload (reward 75, stumped failed, determinism and solution passed): the runs made all six priced stumps (two-ended location, Inland's source change, the solar infeed, the roost survey with the bay fog, conductor heat for grow-ins, each section's deposit from its last wash; R81 to R83), the cause signatures were clean and the washing list held from 0.029 to 0.080 mg/cm2, so every member was forced; architecture 6 is the reviewer's level-up in the same world (the data package, RP-04 and the register kept), with new deciding lessons
lineage.driver: The decisive quantities are where each event happened and what caused it, which no record states: each endpoint instrument computes a position as if the event had no impedance and nothing fed it from the side, so the position comes from how the event's residual flow split between the two endpoints against the network behind each on that date, corrected for a side source that feeds every event beyond it at all hours; the cause comes from conditions measured at the asset by the owner's own sensors and a third party's survey rather than the nearest public station, and from the asset's thermal state rather than the season; and the forward work from a deposit carried from its last reset at each unit's own rate against the level at which it failed before.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each 69 kV fault's location is the split of its residual current between the two terminals solved against the protection study's line-out zero-sequence sources for its date (the 2022 study before Inland's autotransformer replacement in March 2024), with the solar farm's ground infeed taken out of Shell Ridge's distance on the tap line; night faults on the coast are split into fog flashovers, bird streamers and failing strings on the bay stations' dewpoint spread, the roost survey and light rain; summer grow-ins are told by the conductor's temperature on still afternoons; and the sections washed before the fog season are those whose salt deposit, carried from the last wash or soaking rain at the section's own rate, passes the level at which they flashed over.
lineage.stump: The careful but hurried pass locates faults by the relays' own distances on today's study, sets the solar farm's export aside, reads fog off the airport with the roost survey set aside, counts every summer afternoon fault with no stroke as a tree and washes every section that ever flashed over, so it clears the wrong spans, drops Inland's span, puts the tap line's string near Ponder Creek, replaces strings at the roost structures instead of fitting guards, and washes sections cleaned in October while missing four that are due.
